title: Ancestors of `<dfn>` unclear
body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?


I'm implementing a `<dfn>`-element and wanted to read up on how best to do so. In the spec there's the following text:

> The dfn element [represents](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dom.html#represents) the defining instance of a term. The [paragraph](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dom.html#paragraph), [description list group](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/grouping-content.html#the-dl-element), or [section](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dom.html#sectioning-content-2) that is the nearest ancestor of the dfn element must also contain the definition(s) for the [term](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/text-level-semantics.html#defining-term) given by the dfn element.

What made this bit unclear that it mentions `<section>` but links to https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dom.html#sectioning-content-2 (and not https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/sections.html#the-section-element, as one might expect from the text).

This leaves me to question:
- Should (must?) I follow the text, and use an `<section>` as nearest ancestor, or 
- can is use any kind of sectioning content, as the link implies?

Thanks for clarity on this!
